comment_data.body:
Unfortunately, the answer is that there is no way, mostly because of two reasons:
- Allowing them to be properly configurable would require an extra configuration entry for the part which (deliberately) not exposed to the user, i.e. window title and footer content.
- In general I consider both of those parts useful and hiding them will severely affect usability. And adding an option to hide some/all of them is against this.

So I am afraid this part will remain as is.

Sure! Here's my actual code :D

local M = {}
M.state = {
    preview = {
        buf = -1,
        win = -1,
    },
}
M.test_nvim = function(opts)
    opts = opts or {}
    local height = math.floor(0.3 * vim.o.lines)
    local width = math.floor(0.6 * vim.o.columns)
    local buf = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
    local win_cfg = {
        title = "Grep Preview",
        title_pos = "center",
        width = width,
        height = height + 2,
        row = 11,
        col = math.floor((vim.o.columns - width) / 2),
        relative = "editor",
        style = "minimal",
        border = "rounded",
    }
    local win = vim.api.nvim_open_win(buf, false, win_cfg)
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_option(buf, "bufhidden", "wipe")
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf, 0, -1, false, {

        MiniPick.default_preview(),
        -- MiniPick.config.source.preview(),
    })
    return { buf = buf, win = win }
end
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
    pattern = "MiniPickStart",
    callback = function()
        M.state.preview = M.test_nvim { buf = M.state.preview.buf }
    end,
})
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
    pattern = "MiniPickStop",
    callback = function()
        vim.api.nvim_win_close(M.state.preview.win, true)
    end,
})

The problem here is that there is no actual logic about how and when preview should be updated. Plus `default_preview(buf, item)` should be called directly.

Here is a crude prototype which will try preview item every 10 milliseconds:

```lua
local preview_win_id, preview_buf_id, preview_item = nil, nil, nil
local ensure_winbuf = function()
  if not (type(preview_buf_id) == 'number' and vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(preview_buf_id)) then
    preview_buf_id = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
    vim.bo[preview_buf_id].bufhidden = 'wipe'
  end

  if not (type(preview_win_id) == 'number' and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(preview_win_id)) then
    local win_config = {
      relative = 'editor',
      anchor = 'NE',
      width = math.floor(0.3 * vim.o.columns),
      height = math.floor(0.3 * vim.o.lines),
      col = vim.o.columns,
      row = 1,
      style = 'minimal',
      title = 'Preview',
      title_pos = 'center',
      border = 'rounded',
    }
    preview_win_id = vim.api.nvim_open_win(preview_buf_id, false, win_config)
  end
end

local ensure_no_winbuf = function()
  pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_close, preview_win_id, true)
  pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_delete, preview_win_id, { force = true })
end

local preview_timer = vim.loop.new_timer()

local n = 0
local preview_show = vim.schedule_wrap(function()
  local matches = MiniPick.get_picker_matches()
  if matches == nil then
    preview_timer:stop()
    ensure_no_winbuf()
    return
  end

  if vim.deep_equal(preview_item, matches.current) then return end
  preview_item = matches.current
  -- Workaround special preview in `builtin.help`
  if MiniPick.get_picker_opts().source.name == 'Help' then
    pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_delete, preview_buf_id, { force = true })
  end
  ensure_winbuf()

  local preview = MiniPick.get_picker_opts().source.preview
  vim.schedule(function() preview(preview_buf_id, preview_item) end)
end)

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', {
  pattern = 'MiniPickStart',
  callback = function() preview_timer:start(10, 10, preview_show) end,
})
```

It works on most "normal" pickers (like `builtin.files`, `builtin.grep`, etc.), ~but there are some issues with `builtin.grep_live` (as it is inherently special)~. **Edit**: should now also work on latest `main` branch.

If making this preview work 100% of the time will be blocked by some 'mini.pick' implementation details, we can talk about updating those **but** only if there is a working patch which doesn't break existing tests. To be perfectly honest I am not really interested into tracking down source of issues which are only the result of custom "outside" preview.

By the way, I was analyzing each command from MiniExtras for pick.  
When using MiniPick with the preview option enabled, the behavior of the search prompt presents the following issue:

- If I type a valid term, such as `hello` or `print`, MiniPick works correctly and displays the expected results.  
- If I type something that has no matches, such as `xxx`or `xxxxxx`, MiniPick closes automatically instead.  
- Additionally, if I try to delete the invalid text using backspace, MiniPick also closes automatically, without giving me the opportunity to continue typing.

reply_data.body:
> * If I type something that has no matches, such as `xxx`or `xxxxxx`, MiniPick closes automatically instead.
> 
> * Additionally, if I try to delete the invalid text using backspace, MiniPick also closes automatically, without giving me the opportunity to continue typing.

Picker automatically closing is the sign that there was an error. Unfortunately, it is an implementation issue with using `vim.fn.getcharstr()` that properly showing errors is a problem. Debugging this usually involves logging inside custom actions that might provide trouble.

In this particular case, there should be some guard against `nil` previewed item (which is the case when there are no matches).

> I also have a question: How can I add `vim.wo[buf_id].number = true` in the preview? When I open Pick, the preview window doesn’t show the line numbers, but as soon as I move, the numbers appear for a second and then disappear again. Every time I move, the same thing happens—the numbers briefly show up and then disappear. I haven’t been able to fix this behavior.

I don't really understand what you mean by "move" here and which preview do you use here ("native" from 'mini.pick' or separate window). However, the symptoms are similar to setting window's config with `style = 'minimal'`, which will remove line numbers.

> And just out of curiosity, why doesn’t Pick have `WinResized`? In a Linux window manager, when I use a shortcut to resize a window and it becomes floating, Pick doesn’t adjust its size, but Telescope does.

Because `WinResized` is triggered when Neovim's windows are resized. For resizing the whole Neovim instance there is `VimResized` which [is respected in 'mini.pick'](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/939da402095a6ec4229e4de644451cda5bbc3fce/lua/mini/pick.lua#L1962) and does work for me when resizing the whole window in Linux window manager (both interactively and in tests).

> ...
> `config = MiniPick.win_size()`
> ...

This sets window config to a fixed table. The `VimResized` then knows nothing about the logic of `win_size`. Set `config` to the function directly, which will be reevaluated on `VimResized`.

And I'd discourage setting things directly into `MiniPick` table (in this case plain `local` win_size = function() ... end` is enough). Nothing hugely problematic will happen, but the table itself is "owned" by 'mini.pick' module and thus it assumes that only it can make changes to it.
